findings.statement: In the tested native formulation, removing or detaching the shared symmetry reference changes or collapses the tested ordered-triplet behavior.
findings.scope: Tested finite native and comparison representations.
counterevidence: FAT-25 treats reference identity as necessary only within tested constructions.
limitations: No broader model-class search was performed by Acellorator.

findings.statement: For the tested triplet models, equality of an observed slice or closed result was insufficient to establish equality of the pre-closure whole relation.
findings.scope: Tested identity predicates, observed slices, and MTO closure cases.
counterevidence: The result depends on the declared structural identity predicate and tested closure mapping.
limitations: No universal equivalence theorem was established.
Historical phase information may be model-dependent.

findings.statement: The tested perturbations identify symmetry reference, orientation roles, and distinction capacity as a current candidate basis for the modeled triplet identity and dependency behavior.
findings.scope: Finite perturbation and dependency constructions supplied in FAT-25 and FAT-26.
counterevidence: The report does not establish that no simpler or alternative native relation exists.
limitations: OTM completeness and multiplicity remain open.

findings.statement: Within the tested native representation, the three candidate invariants can be named or exposed separately under decomposition, while the tested constructions did not realize them as independent complete relations.
findings.scope: OTM-exposed aspects in the supplied finite computational domain.
counterevidence: A separate model could operationalize the aspects differently without preserving the same native semantics.
limitations: This is a representation-level finding, not an ontological claim.

findings.statement: The tested binary and observational projections lost at least one declared whole-relation distinction under the supplied constructions.
findings.scope: Specific projection and equivalence choices in FAT-23 and FAT-24.
counterevidence: The negative result does not rule out a richer indexed, typed, or higher-arity representation.
limitations: Projection failure is not failure of standard mathematics as a whole.
